limitations: Synthetic scenarios with agent-authored labels. These are development/evaluation checks, not independently human-validated field results.

Requirement-level action, target, retained-detail and exact-source checks are separate from whole-case, grouping and separation checks. A full requirement score does not mean every grouping passed. Software tests are not model-quality scores.
Unanticipated unsupported assertions require semantic review; the automated benchmark does not fully score every possible factual error.
These scenarios use supplied document text and frozen board snapshots. They do not measure scanned-document OCR accuracy or a multi-day field deployment.
Failed runs remain in quality denominators and all-attempt timing. No incorrect merge observed in returned proposals does not establish a universal zero-error rate.
Workflow times include model processing and recorded loading, but exclude human checking/correction. Cold/warm loading and incomplete runs affect direct speed comparisons.
Comparing pipeline versions measures development changes. It does not by itself establish automatic learning or gains from retained reviewer lessons.
Grouping cards is not a measured reduction in unnecessary RFIs. No matched human baseline, actual RFI-submission reduction, or human review-time improvement is established.
Some original scenarios state scope relationships explicitly. The smaller reserved transfer set uses terser wording and fewer hints; all are synthetic, agent-authored cases.

The original V6 separate evaluation had one closure-policy mismatch: a supported negative answer did not preserve unresolved inspection-status work. Review also found an unsupported supersession warning. Original failures remain preserved.

Final V12 informed review found one ambiguously compressed absolute-elevation phrase and one conflict citation list that did not repeat its linked original task-source quotation. That original source remains accessible through the task. Passing the labeled checks does not mean every explanation or evidence display is perfect.

Transfer review found two wording errors outside the labeled routing/detail checks: one reason calls different drawing identities different revisions although both carry revision D; one title says 'by 15:00' where the source says 'before 15:00'. Exact source text and full requirements preserve the correct information. The transfer set has no separate shared-group checks.
